feature.summary: A list of everything the person has published, with name, kind, audience and link, and actions per item. Web has a Sites page (/chat/sites) and a section in Settings. Mobile has a Sites screen with Yours and Shared with you tabs. The CLI has a published command. Names can be changed; there is no description field.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the owner's publications newest first, 200 per page at most, and lets the owner open, copy, rename, share, view versions and data, or take down each one (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:728-763).
purpose.why_it_exists: After publishing, owners need one place to find and manage their links instead of hunting through chats.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who has published; admins checking what a person has shared.
problems_solved: No way to rename a page without republishing.
Needing to find which pages are public.
use_cases: Open Sites to copy yesterday's link.
See which pages are still public.
On mobile, find a site and open its chat.

established.statement: A dashboard lists generated and published sites with state and actions (brief S33.01).
The user can set a name and description for a published app (brief S33.02).
The list is paged with at most 200 per page.
The name is kept when a new version is published, and a name must pass the content policy before saving.
Sites is a ChatGPT and Claude style parity feature set; follow the leaders where it applies.

acceptance_criteria: After publishing two artifacts, the Sites page and Settings list show both, newest first.
The list returns at most 200 rows per page and a cursor when more exist.
Renaming a site changes its title in the list and survives a republish.
A name that violates policy is refused with 'This name cannot be used because it violates the AGI Workforce usage policy.'
On mobile the Yours tab shows the same sites as web for the same account.
CLI published prints each page's audience and link.
A signed-out web visitor sees 'Sign in to manage published artifacts.'

steps.what_happens: Page loads and requests the first page, with a CSRF-free GET and session cookie or bearer token.
Server rate limits (share-view 60 per minute), resolves the user scope, and queries published_artifacts for the owner ordered by creation date.
Client validates the page against the shared schema, rejects duplicates and cursors that do not advance (mobile).
Rename: client PATCH title; server runs moderation and secret inspection, then updates the title.
CLI follows next cursors until done and prints the list.

data.synced: Fetched on demand; web keeps a store, mobile keeps in-memory audiences

data.retained_or_deleted: Updated in place; a version stores the title it was published with.

corrections.claim: CLI published list follows every page cursor and fails on a repeated cursor (artifacts.rs:343-380)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: It follows cursors and errors on a repeated cursor. It is also capped at MAX_PUBLISHED_PAGES = 200 pages and errors with 'did not end within 200 pages' after that. The cap is not mentioned.
corrections.correction: The CLI published list follows page cursors up to 200 pages, fails on a repeated cursor, and fails if the list does not end within 200 pages.

The web strings 'Sign in to manage published artifacts.', 'Loading published artifacts…', 'No published artifacts', 'May be out of date' and 'Failed to load published artifacts' all exist in PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx at 183, 497-544. missing_facts: PATCH on a publication requires a CSRF token before the rate limit, so the claim 'CSRF-free' applies to GET only: apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/route.ts:138-143.
The CLI list is bounded at 200 pages (MAX_PUBLISHED_PAGES): apps/cli/src/cloud/artifacts.rs:31,348,376.

The list is read through getUserScopedDb, so row-level security (forced on published_artifacts) is the access control, not only the user_id filter: apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:133; apps/web/db/neon/0095_published_artifacts.sql:82-92.
